unmatched_reported.note: This is the count-then-insert race that the non-findings list says was knowingly left unfixed.
The limiter key is email|ip and has no account-wide cap, so rotating source IPs gets a fresh budget against the same account each time.
Unknown emails skip bcrypt, so the response-time difference reveals which accounts exist, which the legacy path's simulator prevents.
changePassword does not revoke refresh tokens or stamp session invalidation, so stolen sessions keep working.
The login is stored with its original case but looked up lowercased, so a mixed-case new email locks the user out.
It depends on unverified DTO validation and on how ApiAdvice serialises the context; the reviewer's own text says to verify both.
The caches have no maximumSize and get() stores an entry for every new key, so rotating identifiers grows the heap without limit.
The cache key uses the username as typed, but unlock passes the stored lowercase login, so a mixed-case lock is never removed.
Concurrent requests pass the unlocked existsByUserId check together, and the second hits the unique index and returns a 500.
A failed status load leaves isComplete false, so the guard wrongly redirects a coach whose profile is finished.
